# Feature Specification: Liquid Console Redesign

**Feature Branch**: `014-liquid-console-redesign`

**Created**: 2026-10-31

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User request: "create spec 0014 applying the complete frontend with the design generated by
Claude Code". The generated design is a Claude Design canvas, "Signal Noir UI"
(<https://claude.ai/artifact/BTNyMepHb9VeoTevRfGDQX>), inspired by a soft-surface component sheet and
by a liquid-glass design language, with light and dark modes. Its files are kept beside this spec in
[`design/`](design/) as a **visual reference** (see Reference design, below). Full description:
`docs/specify-prompts/014-liquid-console-redesign.txt`.

## Context

Feature 005 delivered the Operator console: the Case list, the Case detail in six layers with a
Timeline, the approval dialog, the Review Dossier, toasts and the connection note. Its look is the
flat system of the UX spine (`_bmad-output/initiative-signal-noir/ux-signal-noir/DESIGN.md`): warm
paper, borders instead of shadows, system fonts, dark mode only by system preference.

This feature gives **every screen of that console** the new visual language: soft raised and inset
surfaces, liquid-glass layers for what floats, one teal accent, a light and a dark theme the Operator
can switch, and a layout that works from a phone to a wide desktop. It changes how the console looks
and feels. It changes **nothing** about what the console shows, what it sends, or when.

The console's promise stays the one of 005: it never shows a refusal, a replay or an uncertain
outcome as success, and it never changes what is on screen before the server says so. A prettier
surface must not make a doubtful state look calm.

All data is synthetic and every row, header and export says so. UI copy is English.

### Reference design

The files in `design/` are a reference, not a contract:

- `signal.css` carries the tokens and the component styles of the new system, in light and dark.
- `Foundations.dc.html` shows surfaces, color roles, elevation, radius, type and controls in both themes.
- `Main.dc.html` shows one composed Cases screen (shell, summary, queue, detail).

Where the reference and this spec disagree, **this spec wins**. The known differences are listed in
Assumptions (sample data, quick approve, web fonts, summary numbers, extra navigation).

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - The whole console wears the new look (Priority: P1)

An Operator opens the console and every view they can reach looks like one system: the top bar or
rail, the Case list and its rows, the filters, the Case header, the state banner, the six layers, the
Timeline, the approval dialog, the Review Dossier and resolution form, the toasts and the connection
note. No view keeps the old flat look, and no view is left half-converted.

**Why this priority**: A partial redesign reads as a bug. The value is in the console feeling coherent.

**Independent Test**: Open each view against the contract fixtures and check that every surface,
control, chip, tag and message uses the new system (checklist in `checklists/requirements.md`).

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the Case list, **When** it loads, **Then** rows are soft raised surfaces on a quiet
   background, the selected or focused row is clearly distinct, and the filters are one segmented control.
2. **Given** an open Case, **When** it loads, **Then** the header, the single state banner, the six
   layers and the Timeline use the new surfaces, in the same order and with the same content as in 005.
3. **Given** the approval dialog, **When** it opens, **Then** it floats above the page on a liquid-glass
   layer with a visible backdrop, and returns focus exactly as in 005.
4. **Given** a Review Dossier, **When** shown, **Then** it keeps its attention treatment and its place
   (first when `ReviewRequired`, last and collapsed when closed).
5. **Given** a toast or the connection note, **When** shown, **Then** each is a glass layer that never
   covers the control the Operator is using.

---

### User Story 2 - Light and dark, chosen by the Operator (Priority: P1)

The console starts in the theme the Operator's system prefers. A single control in the top bar switches
between light and dark, announces the theme it will switch to, and the choice is remembered in this
browser. Both themes are first-class: every view, state and message is designed and checked in both.

**Why this priority**: Dark and light are an explicit request, and a wrong theme at 3 a.m. is a real cost
for an operations tool.

**Independent Test**: Load with each system preference and with a remembered choice; switch with mouse
and keyboard; compare every view in both themes.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** no remembered choice and a system preference, **When** the console opens, **Then** it uses
   that preference with no flash of the other theme.
2. **Given** the Operator switches the theme, **When** they reload, **Then** the chosen theme is kept.
3. **Given** a remembered choice and a different system preference, **When** the console opens, **Then**
   the remembered choice wins.
4. **Given** the switch control, **When** read by a screen reader, **Then** it says which theme it will
   switch to, and it is reachable and usable by keyboard.
5. **Given** the browser cannot store the choice, **When** the Operator switches, **Then** the theme
   still changes for this session and nothing breaks.
6. **Given** a poll, a dialog or a form in progress, **When** the theme switches, **Then** focus, typed
   values, open sections and inline errors are kept.

---

### User Story 3 - Meaning survives the makeover (Priority: P1)

Every semantic distinction of the UX spine stays visible and stays distinct: observed fact, the
Agent's or rules' interpretation, something waiting for the Operator, a held Case, success, danger,
and "outcome unknown". State is always shown by glyph **and** label, never by color or depth alone.
`SYNTHETIC` and `REPLAY` labels stay on every row and Case header and in the top bar.

**Why this priority**: The soft, low-contrast look of this style makes it easy to lose these
distinctions. They are the product's honesty, so they outrank the style.

**Independent Test**: Render every Case state and every Evidence, Diagnosis and Validator case in both
themes, and check that each pair of meanings can be told apart without color.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** Evidence and a Diagnosis, **When** shown, **Then** fact and interpretation remain
   distinguishable by tag, border style and color, and agent text never appears inside an Evidence card.
2. **Given** any Case state, **When** shown, **Then** it has a glyph and a label, and "Outcome unknown"
   (`Executing` with `reconciling`) is never styled like success.
3. **Given** waiting for approval, review required and uncertain outcome, **When** shown, **Then** each
   keeps its own copy and its own treatment (FR-016 of 005).
4. **Given** a passed and a failed Validator check, **When** shown, **Then** they differ by glyph and
   text as well as color.
5. **Given** a row or a header, **When** shown, **Then** it carries `SYNTHETIC` (and `REPLAY` when it
   applies), in both themes.

---

### User Story 4 - One layout from phone to wide desktop (Priority: P1)

The console adapts to the width of the window without losing a function. At wide widths the
navigation sits beside the content and the Case detail has the layers beside the Timeline. At medium
widths the Timeline moves under the layers and secondary columns of a row drop. On a phone the
navigation becomes a compact bar, rows become stacked cards, and wide tables scroll inside their
own box. There is no horizontal page scroll at 360 px.

**Why this priority**: Reading and approving from a phone is already a 005 requirement; the new
shell must not break it.

**Independent Test**: Render the list, a Case, the dialog and the Dossier at 360, 640, 1100 and 1440
px and check the layout rules and that no function disappears.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** 1100 px or more, **When** a Case is open, **Then** the six layers and the Timeline are
   side by side and the Timeline stays in view while the layers scroll.
2. **Given** 640 to 1099 px, **When** a Case is open, **Then** the Timeline is under the layers and the
   list drops partner and label columns, as in 005.
3. **Given** under 640 px, **When** the list is shown, **Then** each row is a stacked card and the top
   bar wraps without hiding the declared-name field or the synthetic label.
4. **Given** 360 px, **When** any view is shown, **Then** the page has no horizontal scroll, and wide
   tables and raw bodies scroll inside their own container.
5. **Given** the approval dialog on a phone, **When** open, **Then** all of its content and both
   decisions are reachable, and the dialog scrolls inside itself if it is taller than the window.
6. **Given** any width, **When** the Operator uses touch, **Then** every control has a target of at
   least 44 by 44 px.

---

### User Story 5 - Beautiful without making it harder to use (Priority: P2)

The liquid and soft effects degrade gracefully. If the browser cannot blur what is behind a layer, or
the Operator asks for reduced transparency, reduced motion or high contrast, the console stays fully
legible and fully usable with plain, opaque surfaces and clear borders.

**Why this priority**: Glass and soft shadows are the first thing to fail accessibility and the first
thing a low-end screen cannot draw.

**Independent Test**: Run the views with blur unsupported, with reduced transparency, reduced motion
and forced colors, and with the automated accessibility check.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the browser cannot blur the backdrop, **When** a glass layer is shown, **Then** it is
   opaque enough that its text keeps AA contrast.
2. **Given** reduced motion, **When** anything would animate (row changes, highlights, toasts, the
   theme change, spinners), **Then** it does not animate, and a busy state is still shown in text.
3. **Given** forced colors or high contrast, **When** any view is shown, **Then** every control, state,
   focus ring and boundary is still visible.
4. **Given** soft shadows between near colors, **When** a control is shown, **Then** its boundary and
   its focus ring are visible without relying on the shadow.
5. **Given** keyboard navigation, **When** the focus moves, **Then** the focus ring is visible on every
   surface, in both themes, with at least 3:1 contrast against what is around it.

---

### User Story 6 - One visual source of truth (Priority: P2)

The new system is written down once, as named tokens (color roles, surfaces, elevation, radius, type,
spacing, motion) with light and dark values, and the UX spine's `DESIGN.md` is updated to match. A
developer who adds a view gets the look from the tokens, not from copied values, and a reviewer can
see which sections of the old `DESIGN.md` were superseded.

**Why this priority**: Without one source the look drifts view by view.

**Independent Test**: Search the console's styles for color, shadow and radius values outside the
token definitions; read `DESIGN.md` against the shipped look.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the console's styles, **When** searched, **Then** colors, shadows, radii and font stacks
   are defined once and reused by name.
2. **Given** `DESIGN.md`, **When** read, **Then** it describes the shipped system, lists the sections of
   the previous version that are superseded (Elevation & Depth, Shapes, theme behavior, Typography
   limits) and keeps the semantic color meanings.
3. **Given** a new component, **When** added, **Then** it can take its look from the tokens alone.

---

### Edge Cases

- The remembered theme holds an unknown value: the console ignores it and follows the system.
- The system preference changes while the console is open and there is no remembered choice: the
  console follows it live.
- A very long Case, Order or Partner identifier, or a very long exception message, never widens the
  page or overlaps a neighbor; it wraps or truncates with the full value reachable.
- A page with many rows and a lot of glass or shadow still scrolls smoothly on a modest device; the
  number of blurred layers on screen at once is small.
- Text size increased to 200 percent keeps every view usable, with no clipped text or lost control.
- A browser zoom of 400 percent reflows to one column with no loss of function.
- Printing or exporting a Case does not carry the glass or the shadows.
- Offline: the console renders fully with no network request for fonts, images, styles or scripts
  outside the console itself.
- Motion from a poll (a row that changed) never moves a control under the pointer or the focus.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

**Coverage and behavior**

- **FR-001**: Every view of the console (list, Case detail, dialog, Dossier and resolution form,
  toasts, connection note, not-found and empty states, top bar or rail) MUST use the new visual
  system. No view may keep the previous flat look.
- **FR-002**: The redesign MUST NOT change what is shown, what is sent, the polling, the routes, the
  copy, the focus management, the keyboard behavior or any server-answer handling defined in 005
  (FR-001 to FR-018). Every test of 005 MUST pass without edits to its assertions.
- **FR-003**: The console MUST NOT add an endpoint, a field, a route, a state, an Action or a label
  to the contract, and MUST NOT show a number, state or text the contract does not supply.

**Themes**

- **FR-004**: The console MUST offer a light and a dark theme, both complete. With no remembered choice
  it MUST follow the system preference, including live changes.
- **FR-005**: The top bar MUST hold one theme control, operable by keyboard and by touch, whose
  accessible name says the theme it will switch to. The choice MUST be remembered in the browser and
  MUST win over the system preference. The console MUST apply the theme before first paint, with no
  flash of the other theme.
- **FR-006**: If the choice cannot be stored or read, the console MUST work for the session, ignoring
  the failure. An unknown stored value MUST be ignored.
- **FR-007**: Switching the theme MUST NOT reset focus, typed values, open sections, inline errors, a
  dialog or a poll in progress.

**Semantics and honesty**

- **FR-008**: The semantic roles of the UX spine MUST be kept in both themes: accent ("act here"), fact,
  interpretation (also "outcome unknown"), attention, hold, success, danger and focus, each with one meaning.
- **FR-009**: Every state, conflict, failure and check MUST be shown by glyph and label as well as by
  color, and MUST remain distinguishable when depth, shadow and transparency are removed.
- **FR-010**: `SYNTHETIC` MUST stay on every row, every Case header and the top bar, and `REPLAY` where
  it applies, in both themes and at every width.
- **FR-011**: A pill shape MUST stay reserved for Case state chips, so a pill still means "Case state".
  Buttons and other controls MUST use another shape.
- **FR-012**: Floating or glass layers MUST be used only for what sits above the page: the top bar or
  rail, the approval dialog, toasts, the connection note and menus. Content that the Operator reads to
  decide (Evidence, Diagnosis, Proposal, Dossier) MUST sit on opaque surfaces.

**Layout**

- **FR-013**: The layout MUST follow the three bands of 005 (1100 px and up, 640 to 1099 px, under 640
  px): navigation beside the content, then a compact bar; layers beside the Timeline, then the Timeline
  under the layers; list rows as a grid, then fewer columns, then stacked cards.
- **FR-014**: No view may scroll horizontally at 360 px. Wide tables, raw bodies and long identifiers
  MUST scroll or wrap inside their own container and MUST NOT widen the page.
- **FR-015**: Touch targets MUST be at least 44 by 44 px. The shell MUST show only what exists: it
  MUST NOT show navigation entries for screens the console does not have.

**Accessibility, motion and fallbacks**

- **FR-016**: The console MUST keep WCAG 2.2 AA in both themes: text 4.5:1 (3:1 from 24 px or bold 19
  px), non-text boundaries and the focus ring 3:1, keyboard parity, no hover-only action, managed focus
  for dialogs and Evidence jumps, polite live regions for banners and toasts, alerts for inline errors.
- **FR-017**: Glass layers MUST keep AA contrast with and without background blur, and MUST become
  opaque when the Operator asks for reduced transparency or the browser cannot blur.
- **FR-018**: Under reduced motion no animation, transition or smooth scroll may run, and a busy state
  MUST still be conveyed in text. Under forced colors every boundary, control, state and focus ring MUST
  stay visible.
- **FR-019**: Visual changes from a poll MUST NOT move a control under the focus or the pointer, and MUST
  NOT steal focus (FR-014 of 005).

**System of record**

- **FR-020**: Colors, surfaces, elevation, radii, type, spacing and motion MUST be defined once as named
  tokens, with light and dark values, and reused by name. The UX spine's `DESIGN.md` MUST be updated to
  describe the shipped system and to mark the superseded sections.
- **FR-021**: The console MUST need no network request outside itself to render: fonts, icons and
  images ship with it. A font that is not available MUST fall back to a system font with no layout
  break.
- **FR-022**: A printed or exported Case MUST NOT carry glass, blur or shadows and MUST stay legible in
  black on white.

### Key Entities

The redesign owns no data. It restyles the renderings of 005 (CaseListPage, CaseSummary, CaseDetail,
TimelinePage, the approval and resolution results, the error envelope). It adds one browser-side
preference, the theme choice (`light`, `dark`, or none), next to the declared Operator name.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: 100% of the views and states listed in FR-001 are rendered in both themes in the visual
  review, with no view left in the old style.
- **SC-002**: All tests of feature 005 pass with no change to their assertions (FR-002).
- **SC-003**: Automated accessibility checks report no WCAG 2.2 AA violation on the list, the detail,
  the dialog and the Dossier, in light and in dark, at 360, 768 and 1440 px.
- **SC-004**: With color, shadow and transparency removed, an observer tells apart every pair of
  states, and fact from interpretation, in 100% of the review cases.
- **SC-005**: No view scrolls horizontally at 360 px, and no function present at 1440 px is missing
  at 360 px.
- **SC-006**: A reviewer finds no color, shadow, radius or font value used in the console's styles
  outside the token definitions.
- **SC-007**: With reduced motion, reduced transparency and forced colors in turn, every task of
  005's keyboard journey still completes.
- **SC-008**: The console renders completely with the network blocked after the first load.
- **SC-009**: The theme choice survives a reload in 100% of the tests, and no test observes a flash of
  the wrong theme before first paint.

## Assumptions

- **Sample data in the reference is not contract data.** The reference shows invented Cases, Partners
  and Action names (for example `REMAP_TEST_CODE`). The real catalog is `RETRY`,
  `APPLY_APPROVED_MAPPING`, `HOLD` and `REQUEST_REVIEW`, and the real states are those of 005. The
  console shows only what the contract supplies.
- **Quick approve is not adopted.** The reference shows an "Approve proposal" button acting at once.
  The approval dialog of 005 stays: it freezes proposalId and Case version, separates Approve and Deny,
  and requires a reason to deny. The redesign only restyles it.
- **No web fonts from a third party.** The reference loads fonts from a font service. This feature does
  not (FR-021): the console is served by IRIS and works offline. The sans and mono stacks follow the UX
  spine, and the plan may ship font files with the console if it wants a different face.
- **Summary numbers are out of scope unless the contract supplies them.** The reference shows four
  summary counts. Counting only the Cases already loaded would mislead, so the console shows summary
  counts only if the list contract returns totals; otherwise the strip is omitted.
- **Navigation shows Cases only.** The reference lists Orders, Partners, Outbox and Benchmark. Those
  screens do not exist (the Benchmark screen belongs to 010), so they are not shown (FR-015).
- **The Operator's switch is the only new control.** The declared-name field, polling, filters and every
  other control of 005 are unchanged in function.
- **The UX spine changes on purpose.** `DESIGN.md` described a flat system with shadows only on overlays,
  system fonts and a dark mode by system preference. This feature supersedes Elevation & Depth, Shapes
  (buttons no longer share the pill with state chips) and the dark-mode rule, and keeps Colors' meanings,
  Typography's mono-for-literals rule and the Do's and Don'ts.
- Times stay in BRT and copy stays in English, as in 005.
